verses.text: How terrible it will be for the city of bloodshed! It is full of lies and stolen goods, and it never stops robbing its victims.
Listen to the crack of whips and the rumble of wheels! Hear the galloping horses and the bouncing chariots!
Horsemen charge, swords flash, and spears glitter! Many are killed, and the dead bodies are piled high. There are so many bodies that people stumble over them.
All this happened because Nineveh acted like a prostitute, a charming woman skilled in witchcraft. She enslaved nations with her prostitution and peoples with her witchcraft.
"I am against you," says the LORD of Armies. "I will pull your skirts up over your face. I will show the nations your naked body and the kingdoms your shame.
I will throw filth on you and treat you with contempt. I will make you a public example.
Everyone who sees you will run away from you and say, 'Nineveh is in ruins! Who will mourn for her?' Where can I find anyone to comfort you?"
Are you better than the city of Thebes, which sat beside the Nile River with water all around her? The river was her defense, and the water was her wall.
Cush and Egypt gave her endless strength. Put and Libya were her allies.

Yet she was taken captive and went into exile. Her little children were dashed to pieces at the corner of every street. Her enemies threw dice for her nobles, and all her important men were put in chains.
You too will stagger like a drunk. You will go into hiding. You too will look for a safe place from the enemy.
All your fortresses are like fig trees with ripe fruit. When they are shaken, the figs fall right into the mouth of the one who eats them.
Look at your soldiers. They are all weak as women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies. Fire has burned the bars of your gates.
Draw water for the siege! Make your fortresses stronger! Work the clay and trample the mortar! Repair the brick kiln!
But there the fire will burn you up, and the sword will cut you down. It will eat you up like young locusts. Multiply like young locusts! Multiply like swarming locusts!
You have increased the number of your merchants until they are more than the stars in the sky. But like locusts, they strip the land and then fly away.
Your guards are like swarms of locusts, and your officials like clouds of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun comes up, they fly away, and no one knows where they have gone.
King of Assyria, your shepherds are asleep. Your nobles lie down to rest. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
Nothing can heal your wound. Your injury is fatal. Everyone who hears the news about you claps their hands with joy, because everyone has suffered from your endless cruelty.
